findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

I'm approving this executable-red attestation. The attested command exited with code 1, with no signal and no timeout, after 274s against a 600s limit. The expected literal "Required-result refusal must name the exact assertion" appears in the attested full stdout, which was not truncated. Each of the three outline tests (absent, skipped, failed) goes through the scenario's When: the public CLI `proof observe-bounded-delivery` runs on a disposable, committed copy of the full source with one real required assertion changed. Each test checks the scenario's Then. The earlier checks pass: exit code 2, `data.status` of refused, and execution-only authority. Each test then fails only at the step that requires the refusal to name the exact required assertion. The current message, "Fixed runner failed (exit 1, signal null); repair the lane and rerun", gives a rerun action but no assertion name, so the failure is the intended missing behavior at the actor boundary. It is not caused by syntax, imports, fixtures, configuration or infrastructure. I can't recompute the source fingerprint from the packet, so I'm relying on the attestation's binding for it. The findings below are warnings only and don't block approval.

All three outline rows, including 'skipped', reach the observer through the same runner-failure path: 'Fixed runner failed (exit 1, signal null)'. For 'absent', the proof note says the registration test also rejects the renamed declaration. For 'skipped', a lone `it.skip` would normally leave Vitest at exit 0, so the exit 1 means some other test in the lane is failing. That could be the registration control, or an unrelated lane failure such as the stale Codex bundle or the missing basename recorded in the impl plan. A GREEN that grades the report only after a runner failure could pass all three rows without ever showing that a skipped required result is refused when the runner exits 0. Before GREEN credit, record which test makes the 'skipped' run exit nonzero. Also check that a clean, unmodified copy of the same candidate gets a successful runner exit, so the rows test assertion grading rather than a lane that is broken anyway.

The check that the refusal names the right assertion excludes only one other required name, the passing 'persona outcomes' assertion. A message that names the controlled assertion along with several other required assertions that actually passed, other than that one, would still pass. This is acceptable for RED. Consider also checking that no other reviewed required assertion from a passing case is named.

The attestation records parent Node v24.3.0, but the plan pins Node 24.18.1 and `expectResolvedTools` asserts v24.18.1 on the success path. This RED doesn't depend on the version because the CLI runs under Bun 1.3.14. Later GREEN and success-path attestations should run on the pinned Node to avoid a wrong-reason failure.

The steps after the naming check are never reached in this RED run. These include the next-action command, the retained `diagnostic.log` containing the assertion name, and the read-only `verify-bounded-delivery` byte-preservation check. They stay unproven until GREEN.
